Definition: something girt; a belt, also a band
BiblicalUsage: A girdle is the belt a man wore around his waist, and Scripture uses it for readiness, strength, and identity. Elijah is recognised by his girdle of leather about his loins in 2 Kings 1:8, and Jeremiah is told to get a linen girdle and put it upon his loins in Jeremiah 13:1. The prophets also use it as a picture: righteousness shall be the girdle of the Messiah's loins in Isaiah 11:5.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the girdle is a picture of being ready. A man girded his loins to run, to fight, or to work, and I hold that the Christian life is a girded life — truth and righteousness bound close, ready for whatever the day brings.
